source.wing: data/hulls/wing_data.csv borer_wing: 4 craft, INTERCEPTOR role, range 6, built into shepherd.ship
source.ship_data: Borer drone_borer: hitpoints 200, armour 25, speed 200, mass 5, crew 0

units: One sprite pixel per unit about the .ship centre; multiply by metres_per_unit for metres

scale.summary: Crewless mining and utility drone; sized to the Shepherd drone tender's servicing cradle
scale.method: No crew (ship_data crew 0), so no cockpit sets the scale, and the craft has to live on its tender: the Shepherd's open bay carries it on servicing cradles at the three WS 003 launch stations (shepherd-geometry sh_dronebay.py). The cradle deck is 4.84 x 4.37 m with corner chocks 4.2 m apart fore-aft and 3.7 m across, and the bay was laid out for an assumed 4.4 x 4.0 x 1.8 m Borer. The sprite is wider than long (16 x 14 px opaque), so at 0.25 m/unit the drone is 4.0 m across the pods (the assumed span) and 3.5 m long, and stands inside the chocks fore-aft with 0.35 m to spare each end. Its parts agree: a 0.6 m main nozzle and 0.43 m side nozzles for a 5-tonne-class craft (ship_data mass 5), a 0.24 m emitter barrel, a 1.4 m spine. Below 0.22 the spine is too shallow for a reactor and cutting laser; above 0.27 it no longer fits between the chocks.
scale.sprite_disagreement: Measured at the game's own pixel scale the Borer is much bigger: at the Shepherd's 0.78 m/unit it would be 11 x 12.5 m, at the fighters' 0.45-0.55 m/unit about 7 x 8 m (the sprite is 16 px across against the Talon's 22). Neither fits a cradle. The model keeps the cradle; nothing was resized on either side.

sprite.pixel_to_model: col c, row r (from top) covers X 7-r..8-r, Y 8-c..9-c

root.name: Borer root
root.note: the .ship centre: the game's rotation pivot

anchor_convention: ARROWS empties; local +X points along the slot angle (0 = nose, 180 = aft)
notes: Crewless drone (crew 0): no canopy or seat; scale from the tender's cradle (SCALE).
Sprite symmetric about Y = 0 (even width); WS 001 HIDDEN at (0, 0) carries its anchor there and its muzzle at the cutting head's lens on the nose, where the beam leaves the hull.

Engines: main drive on the spine's tail, side drives in the drive pods' slanted aft faces, each face square to its slot angle (160 / 200) so the bell points along the game's exhaust heading. Bell mouths sit on the slot XY for the side drives; the main bell is on the tail face 0.4 units aft of its slot, where the sprite's tail ends. Exhaust anchors are at the mouths, +X down the exhaust.
The four grey points on the sprite's top row are grab tines on the armour pods' noses.

The drive pods hang off the spine on transverse axles (the dark drums between spine and pod on the master) and are braced to the armour pods by a strut and a damper; nothing folds, so there is no deployed/stowed knob. The span (4.0 m) already fits the cradle.
Four fixed pads stand on the cradle deck (parked_check); the belly charging socket sits 12 mm above the cradle's charging contact when the drone is seated.
No lights layer exists for this hull; the only emissives are the two work-lamp lenses and the beacon lens, named as lamps.

silhouette.method: geometry: evaluated triangles projected on XY, 16 samples per sprite pixel, sprite alpha > 0.5; no render (top_silhouette.py)
